text: {"overall_winner":"A","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear three-part structure with introduction, body, and conclusion","quality":"organizational control","description":"The essay presents its ideas in a recognizable argumentative structure that makes the line of reasoning easy to follow."},{"evidence":"explicit claim that driverless cars should not be mass produced","quality":"thesis clarity","description":"The essay states a clear position and keeps returning to it as the central point of the response."},{"evidence":"discussion of cost, driver carelessness, and machine fault","quality":"range of support","description":"The essay offers several distinct reasons against driverless cars instead of relying on only one objection."},{"evidence":"use of a counterargument about reduced accidents and fuel use","quality":"argument balance","description":"The essay acknowledges potential benefits before explaining why the negatives still outweigh them."},{"evidence":"questioning who is responsible if technology fails","quality":"issue awareness","description":"The essay shows awareness of a real consequence of the policy debate by raising liability and safety concerns."}]}
